correctness.rationale: Allu–Kumar's normalization and majorant match this determinant. In their Bernstein certificate the layer M0 has positive weight for y<1 and strictly positive entries; for y=1 and x<1 the support of M2 necessarily includes a positive entry. Hence for c<2 equality requires x=1. Schwarz–Pick boundary rigidity then forces the displayed finite Blaschke form for h; c=2 is separately the Carathéodory extremal. Independent Lagrange inversion and exact rational interpolation reproduce A(c,g), the modulus-defect factorization and both positive Bernstein tables (minimum coefficients 19584 and 19712). For 0<c<2 the defect vanishes only at g=-1; for c=0 a rotation realizes g=-1 from every unimodular g. The resulting logarithmic derivative is the average of two positive-real-part kernels, and the inverse determinant is exactly 1 at every F_c. Each determinant monomial has rotation weight six, and |f''(0)|/2 distinguishes rotation orbits.
